name: ET Katy Pipeline Expansion
researcher_notes: EIA dated August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 586: ET Katy Pipeline Expansion, operator Energy Transfer Co, expansion, completed 6 February 2009, Texas, intrastate, 56 miles, 36 inch, 400 MMcf/d additional capacity, cost 165 (millions) so 165000000 USD. A Natural Gas Intelligence article of 10 October 2007 independently says Energy Transfer Partners would add 56 miles of 36-inch pipe and 20,000 horsepower of compression to its ETC Katy Pipeline, raising capacity from 700 MMcf/d to more than 1.1 Bcf/d, in service by September 2008 (actual completion February 2009 per EIA). That article gives a combined cost of about 260 million USD for two projects, so the cost used is the EIA figure for this project alone. Not an existing GEM row: no ETC Katy or Energy Transfer Katy row is on the roster (Permian Katy, Matterhorn, Traverse, Trident and Mustang are other pipelines). 56 miles is about 90 km, above the 25 km threshold. Intrastate Texas line, so no FERC filing is expected; no Texas Railroad Commission document was checked. Parent system name ETC Katy Pipeline is the name used by the 2007 article; no GEM row exists for the parent, so a parent row may be needed. Start and end locations are not stated in either source and are left blank. Route not found. Owner is the EIA operator Energy Transfer Co, taken as Energy Transfer LP (alias hit in the gazetteer). Proposal year is the 2007 announcement. FID status is inferred from the construction announcement with commitments. Confidence high for length, diameter, capacity and completion; the two sources have different publishers.
